Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 103, verse 1–2:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-ʿAsr (the Time, or Declining Day), because it opens with God's oath by al-ʿAsr, which is the age (al-dahr) and the wonders that it contains.

From the aims of the surah

• To affirm and emphasise that mankind is in loss and ruin, except for those who possess that which saves them: faith and righteous deeds, and mutual counsel to truth and mutual counsel to patience. Within this is an exhortation to the deeds that bring about happiness, and an indication of the ruin of those who are heedless of them.

[The Tafsir]

God swears by al-dahr (the age), because of the wonders of God's power that it contains, which point to His greatness, that the children of Adam are indeed in destruction and deficiency. It is not permissible for a servant to swear except by God, for swearing by other than God is shirk (association of partners with God).

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "the Simplified Exegesis") on Surah 103, verse 3:

Except those who believe in Allah and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to hold fast to the truth, to act in obedience to Allah, and to be patient in that.
